blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Philippine meat imports slowed sharply heading into the late third quarter of 2026, despite overall import volume growing almost 8 percent in the first eight months of the year, according to the Meat Importers and Traders Association (MITA). Data from the Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI) showed that meat imports in August alone declined by 16.1 percent to 115.18 million kilograms, which MITA President Emeritus Jesus Cham said was the lowest monthly arrival volume since April 2024.
